title: A Reminder: Credible Leaders Don't Rely on AI to Compose Their Writing
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership argues that while AI tools offer genuine efficiency for routine communication (meeting summaries, status updates, research briefs), extending that efficiency to symbolic messages -- apologies, crisis responses, strategy pivots, celebrations -- undermines trust. The core distinction is between AI-assisted and AI-authored communication: when an audience evaluates a leader's judgment, sincerity, or conviction, AI-generated writing fails because it draws from 'the average of human expression, untouched by embarrassment, uncertainty, or personal consequence.' In the AI era, audiences increasingly gravitate toward formats impossible to fake: live podcasts, unscripted Q&As, open office hours, whiteboard sessions. Credibility will come not from polished outputs but from demonstrated thinking in motion. Note: Admired Leadership Field Notes are written entirely by humans.
points: * AI is appropriately used for basic communications (meeting summaries, research briefs, distribution emails), but symbolic messages requiring judgment and authenticity must originate from the leader. * 'The primary weakness of generative AI is its tendency to sound correct, conventional, and polished. It draws from the average of human expression, untouched by embarrassment, uncertainty, or personal consequence.' * Authentic leaders build trust by admitting uncertainty, disclosing plans before they're finalized, discussing unresolved challenges, and exploring failures -- the opposite of AI's polished certainty. * Audiences are growing more interested in formats impossible to fake: live podcasts, unscripted town halls, spontaneous Q&As, whiteboard sessions, and open office hours. * In the AI era, credibility comes less from perfectly produced statements and more from 'demonstrated thinking in motion' -- the ability to think under pressure without a script. * 'People do not follow leaders because they sound flawless. They trust and follow them because they sound human enough to believe.'
quotes: Whenever an audience evaluates a leader's character, sincerity, judgment, conviction, or accountability, relying on AI undermines trust.

The primary weakness of generative AI is its tendency to sound correct, conventional, and polished. It draws from the average of human expression, untouched by embarrassment, uncertainty, or personal consequence.

Authentic leaders build trust by doing the opposite. In their writing and speaking, they admit their uncertainty, disclose thoughts and plans before they are finalized, discuss the challenges they face that are still unresolved.
People do not follow leaders because they sound flawless. They trust and follow them because they sound human enough to believe.
In the AI era, credibility for leaders will come less from perfectly produced statements and more from demonstrated thinking in motion.
